grammar.form: reporting verb in the past + reported clause in the present, where the claim still holds
grammar.meaning: keeps a still-true statement true in the reporting

explanation.en: The rule 'past reporting verb, backshift the clause' has an exception every careful writer uses: if the reported thing is still true, the present may stand. 'He told me the office closes at five' — it still does. Backshifting it to 'closed' quietly suggests it no longer does. The choice is meaningful, not stylistic.
explanation.uz: 'Bilvosita nutqda zamonni orqaga suring' qoidasi istisnoga ega: agar aytilgan narsa hamon haqiqat bo'lsa, hozirgi zamon qoladi. 'He told me the office closes at five' — hozir ham shunday.

grammar.positive_example: She explained that water freezes at zero, which the class already knew.
grammar.negative_example: She explained that water froze at zero, which the class already knew.

l1_notes.uz: Rus tilida backshift umuman yo'q, shuning uchun o'quvchi qoidani yo butunlay e'tiborsiz qoldiradi, yo hamma joyda qo'llaydi.

grammar.label: reporting parentheticals and as-clauses
grammar.form: …, he argues, …; as X has shown; as is well known; as noted above
grammar.meaning: attributes a claim without interrupting the sentence that makes it

explanation.en: 'The figures, she argues, were never checked.' The attribution sits inside the sentence, so the claim keeps its shape and the source is still named. 'As Karimova has shown' does the same from the front. The 'as' here is a clause with no object of its own — 'as is well known', never 'as it is well known'.
explanation.uz: 'The figures, she argues, were never checked.' Manba gap ichida ko'rsatiladi, gap esa o'z shaklini saqlaydi. 'As is well known' — 'as it is well known' emas.

grammar.positive_example: The delay, as the committee later conceded, was avoidable.
grammar.negative_example: The delay, as it the committee later conceded, was avoidable.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida manba odatda gap boshida yoki oxirida keladi; gap ichiga joylashtirish yangi ko'nikma.

phonology.label: The glottal stop — t-glottalling across varieties
/h/ dropping in unstressed pronouns — tell him, ask her

functions.label: Reporting an argument without endorsing it

exponents.text: She argues — I am not saying I agree — that the figures were never checked.
The claim, as its author concedes, rests on one letter.
He alleges that the records were altered.
He says the records were altered.

functions.label: Declining formally and leaving the door open

exponents.text: We are not able to take this on this year, though we would welcome it in future.
Regrettably, we must decline on this occasion.
Not this time, but please do ask again.

functions.label: Signalling a change of topic or a digression

exponents.text: While we are on the subject, can I add one thing?
That is a side issue — shall we come back to it?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: You have three sentences in a row that start with 'Karimova says'.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Move the attribution inside. 'The figures, she argues, were never checked.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Then the sentence keeps its own shape.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And the source is still named. You lose nothing.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Here I have 'as it is well known, the road flooded twice'.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Take out the 'it'. 'As is well known' — the 'as' is doing the work of the subject.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Every language I know would put something there.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: English does not, and the extra word is one of the most reliable signs of a foreign hand.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: What about 'he told me the office closes at five'? Kamola says the verb should have moved back.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Does it still close at five?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then leave it. 'Closed' would quietly tell the reader it has changed, and you would not have meant a word of it.
